body.purpose: All data values, descriptions, and content text.

label.purpose: Section headers, panel headers, navigation items, and UI chrome.

shadows.name: trading-card
shadows.purpose: Used on all panels, cards, and dropdowns to create a trading card aesthetic.

motion.name: instant
motion.purpose: Hover states change instantly for game-like responsiveness.

components.name: Panel
components.description: Primary container for content sections with trading card styling.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: #C7D0B8; color: #000; border: 2px solid black; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0px black; padding: 12px; }

components.name: Button
components.description: Game-like button with hard edges and instant hover feedback.
components.css: .ds-button { background: #C7D0B8; color: #000; border: 2px solid black; padding: 4px 8px; font-family: monospace; font-size: 12px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-button:hover { background: #B8C0A8; }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: Monospace uppercase navigation with underline hover.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { font-family: monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: #4b5563; text-decoration: none; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; } .ds-nav-link:hover { text-decoration: underline; color: #000; }

narrative.overview: This system treats players as collectible characters with distinct visual identities, like Pokemon cards in a binder. The interface balances analytical depth with game-like discovery, making data exploration feel like collecting and understanding player archetypes. The aesthetic is intentionally tactile—hard shadows, thick borders, and monospace typography create a physical, game-like quality that makes stats feel like character attributes rather than abstract numbers. The system explicitly rejects the dense, purely numerical interfaces of hoop-reference and BartTorvik. Every metric has a visual counterpart; every data point lives in a context that explains what it means. The monospace font and hard-edged shadows reference retro sports games and trading cards, but the execution is clean and modern rather than dated.
keyCharacteristics: Tactile, game-like UI with hard shadows and thick borders
Pokemon-style player cards as the primary visual metaphor
Monospace typography for a technical, analytical feel
Sage green palette that references basketball courts without being literal
Progressive disclosure: quick lookups first, deep analysis on demand

rules.name: The Hard Border Rule
rules.body: All borders are 2px solid black, no exceptions. No gray borders, no hairlines, no rounded corners.

rules.name: The Trading Card Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are always hard-edged (3px 3px 0px black), never blurred. This creates the feel of physical cards stacked on a surface.

rules.name: The Single Size Rule
rules.body: Typography uses only two sizes: 12px for body and labels, with larger sizes reserved for the logo/title.

rules.name: The Uppercase Label Rule
rules.body: All labels, headers, and navigation items are uppercase with 0.05em letter-spacing.

rules.name: The No Blur Rule
rules.body: Shadows are never blurred. The hard edge is intentional—it makes elements feel physical and game-like.

dos: Use 2px solid black borders on all interactive elements and containers.
Use the Trading Card Shadow (3px 3px 0px black) for all elevation needs.
Keep typography at 12px for body and labels unless it's the logo/title.
Use uppercase with 0.05em letter-spacing for all labels and headers.
Balance numbers with visual explanations—never show raw data without context.
Treat players as characters with visual identities (cards, badges, archetypes).
donts: Use blurred shadows or graduated elevation scales.
Use gray borders or hairlines—black 2px only.
Create interfaces that look like hoop-reference or BartTorvik (dense numbers without visual context).
Use more than two font sizes—keep the uniform, tabular feel.
Introduce new colors beyond the sage palette and black/white/terminal-green.
